items.title: Positive-gamma calm-up cluster across breadth, dealer positioning, and flow
items.note: Three independent surfaces line up bullish-but-contained: heatmap breadth is broad at 65.06% of 134 names, SPY dealers sit in positive gamma with the flip at 773.14 beneath the 777/780 wall band, and unusual options flow is call-heavy at 82% (call fraction 0.8163). Positive dealer gamma plus broad breadth argues for a pinned, mean-reverting drift toward the 777-780 walls rather than a trend-day breakout, and with spot 778.56 already wedged between the walls and just above VWAP 778.09, strength chased into the call wall carries less edge than fades of extremes back toward VWAP.
items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth metric, the options-structure and gamma dealer regime with its wall levels, and the options-flow lean, then reconcile them against the intraday VWAP and spot to judge whether the up-tilt is a trend impulse or a gamma pin.

items.title: Equity and tech risk-on drains real assets while a defensive sector leads rotation
items.note: Sector rotation is into XLC as XLE weakens and ETF momentum is led by tech (VGT 34.69%) with breadth broad, yet the real-assets book is broadly weak: silver (SLV) 14.6 and gold (GLD) 38.7 are mixed-to-soft, bitcoin (BTC-USD) 34.2 is in a downtrend, broad commodities (DBC) 51.0 and oil (USO) 43.6 are middling, and only industrial copper (CPER 56.3) sits near the top. The divergence reads as an equity and tech risk-on advance rather than a reflation or hard-asset hedge bid, so real-asset vehicles are a poor confirmation source and a weak diversifier this window.
items.method: Compare the sector rotation into/out tickers and the ETF-momentum leader against the real-assets model scores and trends, flagging the sign divergence between equity leadership and hard-asset momentum.
